properties.description:
A combination of dry and breezy conditions today will result in
an elevated risk of wildfire spread across most of central
Pennsylvania. The ongoing dry spell combined with minimum relative
humidity values around 30 percent this afternoon and wind gusts
from the northwest between 20 and 30 mph will all contribute to
the elevated risk of wildfire spread.

Residents are urged to exercise caution if handling any potential
ignition sources, such as machinery, cigarettes, or matches.
If dry grasses and tree litter begin to burn, the fire will have
the potential to spread rapidly.

For more information about wildfire danger and wildfire
prevention and education, please visit the Pennsylvania Department
of Conservation and Natural Resources website at
http://dcnr.pa.gov/Communities/Wildfire.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 7:50AM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
There is an elevated risk for fire spread today across eastern
Pennsylvania. Minimum relative humidity values will drop to
around 35 percent this afternoon. This will be accompanied by
temperatures rising generally rising into the 60s and 70s and
west winds around 10 to 15 gusting to around 25 mph. These
conditions could support the rapid spread of any fires that
ignite, which could quickly become difficult to control.
Conditions improve during the evening as the wind diminishes and
the relative humidity increases.

Outdoor burning is strongly discouraged. Be sure to properly
extinguish or dispose of any potential ignition sources, including
smoking materials such as cigarette butts. Use caution while
using any machinery outdoors, such as lawn care equipment, that
could cause sparks to come in contact with the dry ground.

This forecast considers meteorological, fuel, and land conditions
and has been developed in coordination with state fire officials.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED RISK FOR FIRE SPREAD TODAY

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 29 at 2:39PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
ESFABQ

* IMPACTS...River, creek, washes and arroyos may reach out of
banks. Rock, mud and debris may flow into roadways and flash
flooding can not be ruled out, especially in urban areas.

* CONFIDENCE...High confidence in widespread rainfall, with low
confidence in river and flash flooding.

* WHAT...A strong Pacific storm system will interact with a
atmospheric river streaming into the Desert Southwest and Four
Corners region, producing widespread rain which will focus in
the mountains.

* WHERE...Four Corners and surrounding region, including Aztec,
Bloomfield, Farmington and Shiprock.

* WHEN...Sunday into Monday.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...River basins are already saturated from
last week's rainfall and flooding, making additional runoff more
efficient and can more easily cause flooding problems. The
greatest precipitation amounts are forecast in the San Juan
Mountains of Colorado, which will create high flows in the
Animas and La Plata Rivers. These rivers feed the San Juan
River, which saw record flooding last week.

Continue to monitor forecasts for the updates as this situation
unfolds.

and on X at: www.x.com/NWSAlbuquerque

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 29 at 3:13PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
The combination of dry fuels, gusty northwest winds 20 to 30 mph,
and minimum relative humidity values near 40 percent will lead to
an elevated risk of fire spread across the Lower Hudson Valley
during the late morning and afternoon on Friday.

Use extra caution if handling any potential ignition sources such
as machinery or matches, and ensure to properly extinguish or
dispose of cigarette butts. Any fires that ignite will have the
potential to spread quickly.

This forecast considers meteorological, fuel, and land conditions
and has been developed in coordination with state fire and land
management officials.

For more information about wildfire danger and wildfire
prevention, please visit the New York Department of Environmental
Conservation website at...
https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/wildfires.
